newsitem.title: UK: BoE's George warns of dispute with Germany, France.
newsitem.headline: BoE's George warns of dispute with Germany, France.

text.p: Bank of England governor Eddie George warned in an interview with the Financial Times that the dispute among Britain, Germany and France over access to the future Target EU interbank payment system threatened to undermine co-operation among Europe's central banks.

In his first public statement on Target, he called the dispute trivial in itself but added: "For the first time something was being introduced into the EMU (European Monetary Union) discussion which was discriminatory for a non-monetary reason."
"We are not in the business of compromise over Target -- we are taking about principle," he said.
He stressed the need for constructive co-operation between European Central banks in the European Monetary Institute.

"I don't see why the situation should develop into a split between the ins and the outs. But you could see that developing if the ins felt they were imposing on themselves a discipline which is not going to apply to the others."
He said European Monetary Union could be even "an absolutely huge opportunity" for the city of London. "I think the potential pluses are very considerable in relation to the potential minuses."
But then he added: "I am making two assumptions about that. Firstly, that we are technically ready, which I see no reason at all why we won't be.
"The second is that negotiations continue in a constructive, mutual kind of way."
He told the paper: "I don't think there is a loss of leverage for the UK at the moment. If you have a valid point to make, everyone has been prepared to listen to it."
